summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, cardiomyopathy due to Chagas disease, and a history of coronary artery bypass grafting was admitted for acute gallstone pancreatitis. He presented with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting, and was found to have elevated lipase and gallstones on ultrasound. He was managed conservatively with IV fluids and pain control while optimizing his blood pressure with increased lisinopril and addition of isosorbide mononitrate for surgical clearance. He underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, during which he experienced transient bradycardia and a temporary junctional rhythm that resolved without intervention. Postoperatively, he had mild nausea but tolerated a regular diet and recovered well. His medications were adjusted, including continuation of Imdur and increased simvastatin, while reverting to his prior lisinopril dose. He received hemodialysis as scheduled and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans.
